case: David Tepper buying distressed U.S. banks during the 2009 crisis

source_summary.setup: During February and March 2009, many investors feared that large U.S. banks could be nationalized and that common shareholders could be wiped out.
source_summary.policy_signal: The Treasury Department introduced the Financial Stability Plan, including a stated commitment to inject capital into banks through preferred-stock purchases.
source_summary.variant_view: Tepper interpreted the written government plan as a credible backstop: the government had stated how it would support the banks, and the market was not fully believing it.
source_summary.market_behavior: Bank shares and preferreds kept collapsing after the plan. Bank of America traded below $3, Citigroup preferred traded below $1, and many investors were unwilling to bid.
source_summary.instruments: Appaloosa bought a mix of bank common equity, preferred shares, debt, and related distressed credit.
source_summary.risk_debate: Skeptical investors and partners worried that more carnage was coming, nationalization could wipe out common equity, and bank debt or preferreds were safer than common shares.
source_summary.positioning: Tepper bought through severe fear and mark-to-market pressure, then added more when banks later raised capital and the thesis was confirming.
source_summary.outcome_context: By late March 2009, Citigroup common had tripled from its lows, and broader bank and junk-bond holdings were rising. This later outcome is useful for grading but should not be treated as known at the decision date.

selected_details: Bank of America common traded below $3 during the panic.
Citigroup preferred shares traded below $1 during the panic.
Bank of America reached an indicated low around $2.53 on 2009-02-20.
Citigroup common traded as low as $0.97 by 2009-03-05.
The market fell sharply on the day Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner introduced the plan.
Tepper estimated roughly a 20% chance of nationalization for banks such as Citigroup.
Tepper viewed the written government support plan as legally and politically difficult to ignore.
